---
title: "Get started with zuhttp"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Every chunk talks to a real public API, so the output below is what the
# service returned when the site was built. error = TRUE keeps one service
# being down from failing the whole site build.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = TRUE)
```

This article walks through the requests most scripts need: fetching a page,
reading the response, and sending data in the two shapes APIs ask for, JSON
and forms. Every example is a real request against a public API that needs no
key.

```{r setup}
library(zuhttp)
```

## Make a request

`zu_get()` sends a request and returns the response. A status of 400 or above
raises an error, so a response you hold is one that succeeded.

```{r get}
r <- zu_get("https://httpbin.org/get", query = list(q = "zuhttp", page = 2))
r
```

The `zu_resp_*()` functions read the parts of a response:

```{r resp}
zu_resp_status(r)
zu_resp_url(r)
zu_resp_header(r, "content-type")
str(zu_resp_json(r)$args)
```

`zu_resp_text()` gives the body as a string, decoded with the response's
charset, and `zu_resp_raw()` gives the bytes.

## Send JSON

`zu_post()` sends a body. With `json =` the list is serialised for you and
`Content-Type: application/json` is set. httpbin echoes back what it
received, which shows what went over the wire:

```{r echo}
r <- zu_post(
  "https://httpbin.org/post",
  json = list(name = "Alice", package = "zuhttp")
)
str(zu_resp_json(r)$json)
zu_resp_json(r)$headers[["Content-Type"]]
```

Most REST APIs create a resource from a JSON body and answer `201 Created`
with the new record:

```{r create}
r <- zu_post(
  "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts",
  json = list(title = "hello", body = "world", userId = 1)
)
zu_resp_status(r)
str(zu_resp_json(r))
```

The response need not be JSON. GitHub's Markdown API, which needs no token,
takes JSON and returns HTML:

```{r markdown}
r <- zu_post(
  "https://api.github.com/markdown",
  json = list(text = "**hello** _world_", mode = "markdown")
)
zu_resp_text(r)
```

## Send a form

Some APIs want `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` instead. Pass `form =` and
zuhttp encodes the fields. Here is a search on Wikipedia's API:

```{r form}
r <- zu_post(
  "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php",
  form = list(
    action = "query",
    list = "search",
    srsearch = "R language",
    srlimit = 3,
    format = "json"
  )
)
hits <- zu_resp_json(r)$query$search
vapply(hits, function(hit) hit$title, character(1))
```

`zu_put()`, `zu_patch()` and `zu_delete()` take the same `json =`, `form =`,
`body =` and `file =` arguments.

## Handle failure

A failed request raises a condition you match by class, not by parsing its
message. An HTTP error carries the response:

```{r failure}
tryCatch(
  zu_get("https://httpbin.org/status/404"),
  zu_http_client_error = function(e) zu_resp_status(e$response)
)
```
